name: Learning from limited labels
gist: Papers on training models when you have few labeled examples, by actively choosing which data to label, learning from unlabeled data, or using synthetic data.
explain: Labeling data by hand is expensive and slow. A doctor labeling medical images, a translator labeling text, a quality engineer labeling defects — all of this takes human time. Yet many machine learning models need thousands or millions of labeled examples to work well. The question is: can you learn from a much smaller set of labeled data by being smart about which examples you ask a human to label, or by using unlabeled data to fill in gaps?

The hard part is that the model has to learn patterns from a tiny set of labeled examples, which means it easily memorizes the examples instead of learning the real pattern. It is also hard to know which examples to label. If a human labels 100 examples picked randomly, it is inefficient — some will be easy and tell the model nothing new. You need to focus on the examples that teach the most: the ones the model is uncertain about, or the ones that represent patterns the model has not seen before.

Researchers approach this through multiple strategies. Active learning systems identify which examples a human should label to maximize learning — for example, by asking about examples where the model is most uncertain. Semi-supervised learning uses unlabeled data: the model trains on labeled data, then looks for patterns in unlabeled data that are consistent with what it learned (for example, if the model learned that images of dogs have pointy ears, it can cluster images by ear shape even without labels). Self-supervised learning creates labels automatically by hiding part of the data and asking the model to predict it (for example, hiding one word in a sentence and training the model to predict the word, which teaches it about language). Some researchers even use synthetic data — generating fake labeled examples that have the same patterns as real ones — to supplement scarce real labels.

papers.title: Deploying Models to Non-participating Clients in Federated Learning without Fine-tuning: A Hypernetwork-based Approach
papers.contribution: HyperFedZero consistently outperforms competing federated learning methods with minimal computational, storage, and communication overhead.

papers.title: Exposing Mixture and Annotating Confusion for Active Universal Test-Time Adaptation
papers.contribution: Active Universal Test-Time Adaptation significantly improves performance and achieves state-of-the-art results by strategically annotating high-uncertainty regions.

papers.title: Learning from Synthetic Data Improves Multi-hop Reasoning
papers.contribution: LLMs fine-tuned on synthetic data significantly outperform on real benchmarks, demonstrating synthetic data teaches fundamental generalizable reasoning skills.

papers.title: Privacy-Protected Causal Survival Analysis Under Distribution Shift
papers.contribution: Method demonstrated validity and efficiency gains on multi-site HIV prevention trials and all-cause mortality analysis.

papers.title: Robust LLM Unlearning via Post Judgment and Multi-round Thinking
papers.contribution: PoRT demonstrates superior robustness against adversarial attacks and strong unlearning effectiveness without compromising general model utility.

papers.title: Deep Latent Variable Model based Vertical Federated Learning with Flexible Alignment and Labeling Scenarios
papers.contribution: Unified framework handles arbitrary alignment, unlabeled data, and multi-party collaboration, outperforming baselines in 160/168 configurations.

papers.title: FSPO: Few-Shot Optimization of Synthetic Preferences Effectively Personalizes to Real Users
papers.contribution: Achieves 87% Alpaca Eval win-rate on synthetic users and 70% win-rate on real users in open-ended QA with strong transfer from synthetic to real data.

papers.title: MobileKGQA: On-Device KGQA System on Dynamic Mobile Environments
papers.contribution: Achieves 20.3% higher performance on Jetson Orin Nano while using only 30.4% of SOTA energy, with 7.2% computation and 9% parameters on standard benchmarks.

papers.title: Preserve and Sculpt: Manifold-Aligned Fine-tuning of Vision-Language Models for Few-Shot Learning
papers.contribution: Significantly improves performance while preserving semantic manifold structure in few-shot image classification.

papers.title: The Signal is in the Steps: Local Scoring for Reasoning Data Selection
papers.contribution: LALP enables selecting best teacher and curating diverse pools; improves accuracy selecting natural solutions by large margin across math, coding, science tasks.

papers.title: Transitive Representation Learning Enhances Histopathology Annotation
papers.contribution: *SpatialWhisperer* outperforms published baselines, achieving relative AUROC gains of up to 15

papers.title: Unifying and Optimizing Data Values for Selection via Sequential Decision-Making
papers.contribution: Unifies existing data valuation methods through DP lens and proposes bipartite-graph surrogate enabling scalable greedy selection with provable guarantees.
